Hence, up to symmetry,
\[
G=(\Psi_1\cup B)+af.
\]

Put $H_0=B+ac+cd+bd$. By Lemma~\ref{dis:joint-test}, $G$
is toroidal if and only if $H_0$ is planar. Indeed, the
simple-face test for $P_1,P_2$ contains $H_0$, and the
choice $(1,2,2)$ has no face for $af$. For $(2,1,1)$,
the repeated-face test is $H_0$, while $af$ lies in a
simple face for $P_1,P_3$, whose test graph is a
four-cycle with a diagonal. The same argument applies
with any allowed minor in place of $B$.

The graph $H_0$ is a minor of $G$, using $apc$ and $brd$
for $ac$ and $bd$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. It is
nonplanar, since $G$ is nontoroidal, and therefore
contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision. Apply
Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with attachments
$A$ and added edges $E=\{ac,cd,bd\}$. It gives an
allowed minor $B'$ with at most nine interior vertices
and $B'+E$ nonplanar. The preceding equivalence makes
$(\Psi_1\cup B')+af$ nontoroidal, so minimality forces
$B'=B$.

Thus $B$ belongs to the finite family of
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} with
attachments $A$, added edges $E$ and no required edges.
Every resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor or a proper
nontoroidal minor obtained by deleting or contracting
one edge~\supp{E3}, a contradiction.

The candidates are the graphs B of Construction 3.16 with attachments A, added edges E = {ac, cd, bd} and no required edges: A independent in B, interior nonempty and connected, every attachment with an interior neighbour, and B + E nonplanar (each candidate gives a Kuratowski subgraph).
verdicts: Every candidate gets a proper nontoroidal minor obtained by deleting or contracting one edge of G (a contraction merges the second vertex into the first). The witness says why that minor is nontoroidal.
